intro_cards.title: About these notes
body: 8 units · tectonics to contours

Grade 12 is “geography of Eritrea in depth”. Grade 11 is the toolkit: how the crust moves, how water and wind carve, how people settle, then a first look at Eritrea’s place, relief and contour maps. Read each unit as a *story with a cause* — examiners mark the cause, not only the landform name.

intro_cards.title: Worked contour gradient
body: Two points: 1 200 m and 1 000 m. Map distance between them is 4 cm. Scale 1:50 000 (1 cm = 500 m).
Rise = 200 m. Run = 4 × 500 = 2 000 m. Gradient = 200/2000 = 1 in 10 (or 10%). Write both the fraction and a sentence: “For every 10 m walked horizontally you climb 1 m.”

units.title: Relief and Drainage Patterns in Eritrea

f2.title: Tap-level sketch (same idea as Grade 12). East drainage to the Red Sea; west to Sudan; some streams die in Danakil.

cards.title: Relief — five belts to be able to sketch
body:
1. **Western lowlands** — broad, hot, falling toward Sudan. Sorghum / pastoral country; rivers like Barka and Gash.
2. **Highlands** — the spine. Cooler, more densely settled, rain-fed cereals. Asmara sits here.
3. **Eastern escarpment** — a steep drop toward the sea. Orographic moisture can make this the greenest strip; roads zigzag.
4. **Coastal plain** — narrow, hot, humid to arid depending on stretch; Massawa and the ports.
5. **Danakil / southern depression** — below or near sea level in parts, extreme heat, salt, rift geology (tie back to Unit 1).

The highlands are divided into six land features.
Hager Nues being 2770m.a.s.l. is the highest peak in this highland region.
The region has limited importance for agriculture because of the absence of thick soils.

cards.problem: By what percentage does water volume expand when it undergoes freezing inside rock crevices?

steps.text: Liquid water transitioning into crystalline solid ice undergoes volumetric expansion.
Water volume expands by exactly $$10\%$$ upon freezing, producing the destructive pressure responsible for frost wedging.

cards.title: Worked from review
cards.problem: What is the geomorphic term for the physical weathering process in which concentric rock shells peel off due to diurnal thermal expansion and contraction?

steps.text: The process involves rock sheets peeling off in concentric layers parallel to the surface.
This is caused by daily solar heating (expansion) and nightly cooling (contraction) in arid environments, structurally defined as exfoliation.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Which of the following is categorized as an external, gradational geomorphic force?
cards.why:
**Step 1: Distinguish geomorphic forces**
Internal (endogenous) forces build up topography from inside. External (exogenous) forces wear down topography from outside.

**Step 2: Categorize options**
Volcanism, faulting, and folding are internal tectonic forces. Running water is an external gradational force.

**Step 3: Final Result**
The correct exogenous agent is **Running water**.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The narrow, shallow channel cut in soil at a river's source is called a/an:
cards.why:
**Step 1: Trace river source structures**
At a river's headwaters, rainwater initially accumulates in tiny channels.

**Step 2: Identify channel dimensions**
These tiny channels, about $$5\text{ to } 8\text{ cm}$$ deep, are defined as rills.

**Step 3: Final Result**
The correct term is **Rill**.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: By what percentage does water volume expand when it undergoes freezing inside rock crevices?
cards.why:
**Step 1: Recall frost action parameters**
Liquid water transitioning into crystalline solid ice undergoes volumetric expansion.

**Step 2: Identify expansion percentage**
Water volume expands by exactly $$10\%$$ upon freezing, producing the destructive pressure responsible for frost wedging.

**Step 3: Final Result**
The expansion is **$$10\%$$**.

cards.title: Tap-level sketch (same idea as Grade 12). East drainage to the Red Sea; west to Sudan; some streams die in Danakil.
Drainage — three stories, not one national river
body: **Eastern system:** short, steep catchments racing down the escarpment to the Red Sea. Flashy after rain; little room for long flood plains.
**Western system:** longer rivers (Barka, Anseba, Gash–Mereb, Setit on the border) that drain toward Sudan. More useful for alluvial farming where the bed is wide, still seasonal.
**Danakil interior:** some streams never reach the sea; they evaporate or sink in the depression. Endorheic = closed basin.
Lakes in Eritrea are few and often seasonal or coastal / lagoonal rather than great inland seas. Do not invent a “Lake Victoria of Eritrea” on the paper.

cards.title: 7.2.2 The western drainage system
body: The longest tributary of the river Anseba is River Zara, which originates from Halhal Highlands.
The river Anseba joins river Barka close to the Sudanese border at Sala where both drain into the Sudan.

body: Many of the rivers that drain into the Danakil Depression dry up in the sandy surface.

cards.title: Worked: highland advantage
cards.problem: One farming advantage of Eritrean highlands?

steps.text: Cooler temps / often more reliable rains than coastal desert (as in notes).

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The rivers of Eritrea that drain into **Danakil Depression** are:
cards.why: The Danakil (Internal) drainage system consists of rivers that do not reach the sea but disappear in the Danakil Depression. Major rivers in this system include the **Endeli** and **Dandero**.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Which one of the following rivers **does not** drain to the east?
cards.why: In Eritrea, rivers like Alighede, Haddas, and Labka drain East into the Red Sea. The **Aderbabo** river is part of the western drainage system, flowing toward the Gash/Barka system and eventually toward Sudan.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Which of the following rivers of Eritrea, flows eastward?
cards.why: Rivers like Gash, Barka, Anseba, and Mereb flow westward or northward towards the Nile basin or the Sudanese plains. River Labka, originating from the eastern escarpments, flows eastward into the Red Sea.

cards.title: 7.3 Lakes in Eritrea
body: In Eritrea, there are no significant natural lakes.
Lake Bordole is located in the Buri Peninsula where salt is extracted.
Lake Bada and Lake Aba Adad are found in the Danakil Depression.
All are salty lakes, which carry water during the rainy season and dry up during the dry season.
Depositions are found in the lower sections of the river courses.

cards.title: Where, how big, why it matters
body: The administrative regions (zobas) are the structure you use when you locate a case study (highlands vs Northern / Southern Red Sea vs Gash-Barka vs Anseba, etc.). You do not need to memorise every boundary — you need to know *which belt* a named town sits in.

tips.text: The present relief of Eritrea is highly diversified and consists of different types of features that include mountain ranges, deep gorges, plains and offshore islands.
The country’s relief is broadly divided into three major divisions. These are the Highlands, the Lowlands and the Escarpments.
The Highlands extend from south to north.
The Northern Highlands are very much dissected by major river systems such as River Anseba.
The Central Plateau occupies geographically important location as major rivers of Eritrea originate from this plateau.

The Southern Plateau is agriculturally rich because of its flat terrain, adequate rainfall and fertile soil. There are two major divisions of lowlands. These are the Eastern Lowlands and the Western Lowlands.
Eritrea has a drainage system, which is divided into three major groups: The Eastern Drainage System, Western Drainage System and rivers that drain into the Danakil Depression.
Most of the rivers are seasonal in character with high erosive power due to the steep slopes.

questions.q: Eastern escarpment of Eritrea is typically
why: Answer D: Steep and relatively green
The eastern escarpment drops steeply from the highlands to the coastal plain; moist air from the Red Sea gives it rain in winter, so it is relatively green (e.g. around Filfil).

questions.q: Which of the following rivers **does not** flow towards the Red Sea?
why: The **Anseba River** flows northwards and is a major tributary of the Barka River. The Barka-Anseba system flows towards the plains of Sudan (Western Drainage). Rivers like Alighede, Hadas, Felket, and Labka flow eastward into the Red Sea (Eastern Drainage).
questions.tip: Read every option before choosing; rule out the ones that contradict the notes.

questions.q: One of the following rivers **does not** drain towards the east.
why: The Mereb River (known as the Gash in its lower course) flows westward toward the Sudanese plains. Rivers like Felket, Labka, Haddas, and Comayle all drain eastward into the Red Sea.
questions.tip: Read every option before choosing; rule out the ones that contradict the notes.

questions.q: Which one of the following Eritrean Rivers enter to the Red sea through **Marsa Teklay**?
why: The **Labka** river is one of the seasonal rivers in the eastern drainage system of Eritrea that flows into the Red Sea near **Marsa Teklay**.
questions.tip: Read every option before choosing; rule out the ones that contradict the notes.

questions.q: Which of the following major rivers in Eritrea originates from west of Asmara around Adi Guadad and Mai Nefhi and flows toward western lowland?
why: River Barka originates in the central highlands of Eritrea, specifically in the areas west of Asmara near Adi Guadad. It flows in a northwesterly direction through the western lowlands toward the Sudanese border.
questions.tip: Read every option before choosing; rule out the ones that contradict the notes.

questions.q: Which one of the following is **not** tributary of Mereb River?
why: The **Belessa** river is a major tributary of the **Tekeze** (Setit) river system. Ubel, Gala, and Tsorena are all tributaries that feed into the Mereb-Gash system.
questions.tip: Read every option before choosing; rule out the ones that contradict the notes.

questions.q: A highland relief which is characterized with the highest elevation in Eritrea is
why: The **Eastern Plateau** (or Eastern Escarpment) contains the highest peaks in Eritrea, including **Emba Soira**, which is the highest point in the country at approximately 3,018 meters above sea level.
questions.tip: Read every option before choosing; rule out the ones that contradict the notes.

questions.q: Which one of the following rivers **do not** pass through the Gulf of Zula to enter the Red sea?
why: The Gulf of Zula is a major inlet of the Red Sea in Eritrea. Rivers like Alighede, Haddas, Comayle, and Siyah-gede drain into this specific gulf. The Labka river, however, drains into the Red Sea further north, near the Massawa area, and does not pass through the Gulf of Zula.
questions.tip: Read every option before choosing; rule out the ones that contradict the notes.

why: Belessa, Ubel, Ambessa, and Balwa are known tributaries of the Mereb-Gash river system. **Gala** is a tributary associated with the Barka-Anseba drainage system.
